meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'строение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'mood, attitude' in everyday Russian.

Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'строение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'mood, attitude' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: С таким настроением, конечно, не будет.
examples.trans: With an attitude like that, of course there won't be.

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву.
examples.trans: Go to Anikeev in just that mood.

meanings.note: impersonal with dative: мне/вам хочется = I/you feel like, really want

examples.text: Я понимаю, вам очень хочется квартиру.
examples.trans: I understand you really want the flat.

examples.text: Самсоновы, ну вы очнитесь! Я понимаю, вам очень хочется квартиру.
examples.trans: Samsonovs, come to your senses! I understand you really want the flat.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Food or pizza delivery place. Common feminine noun meaning 'pizza' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free.

examples.text: Анатолий Иванович, тут доставка пиццы. Пишут, доставим за десять минут.
examples.trans: Anatoly Ivanovich, there's pizza delivery here. They write: we'll deliver in ten minutes.

meanings.note: On foot. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

поднять.gloss: to lift, to raise; to rouse

meanings.note: 'поднять людей' = to get people moving
'поднять людей' = to get people moving

examples.text: А я глаза на это закрывать не буду. Я подниму людей!
examples.trans: Well, I'm not going to close my eyes to this. I'll rally people!

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'знакомиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to meet, to get acquainted', paired with 'знакомиться'.

examples.text: А как вы с ней познакомились?
examples.trans: And how did you meet her?
She was the one who met me!

examples.text: Это она со мной познакомилась! Ходила вокруг меня, как акула.
examples.trans: She was the one who met me! She circled around me like a shark.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

вообще-то.gloss: actually, as a matter of fact

meanings.en: actually, as a matter of fact, for the record
meanings.note: Polite or pointed correction. Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще-то'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Меня вообще-то Юля зовут. Вот сахар.
examples.trans: My name is actually Yulia. Here's the sugar.

meanings.note: short forms знаком, знакома, знакомо, знакомы (+ dative)

examples.text: А знакомо ли тебе, Аркашка, слово педикюр?
examples.trans: And are you familiar, Arkashka, with the word pedicure?

examples.text: Я услышал в коридоре знакомый голос.
examples.trans: I heard a familiar voice in the corridor.
I will call acquaintances right now.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.
Core Russian interj meaning 'stop!, cut!' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Stop, you cannot go any further!
Stop, that's a wrap! Good job, Samson!

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Это просто = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
Also 'girlfriend' (моя девушка). Common feminine noun meaning 'young woman; girlfriend' in everyday Russian.
Своя девушка. Common feminine noun meaning 'young woman; girlfriend' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: 'на работе' = at work. Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
Agreeing, often reluctantly. Core Russian part meaning 'all right, OK' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Садитесь = sit down (polite). Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'адиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sit down', paired with 'сесть'.

examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: Direction. Core Russian adv meaning 'here (to this place)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: Удобнее = more comfortable. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'добный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('comfortable; convenient').

Удобное время = convenient time. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'добный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('comfortable; convenient').

examples.trans: Allow me, I'll make it more comfortable.
This is a very comfortable armchair.

examples.text: Прошу, присаживайтесь. Позвольте, я сделаю удобнее.
examples.trans: Please, have a seat. Allow me, I'll make it more comfortable.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (on foot)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.
What did you bring into the flat?

выпить.gloss: to drink (up); to have a drink

meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink of
meanings.note: + accusative or partitive genitive. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drink (up); to have a drink', paired with 'пить'.

Used without an object. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drink (up); to have a drink', paired with 'пить'.

examples.trans: May I drink a tiny drop of beer?

examples.text: Милый, можно я выпью капельку пива?
examples.trans: Darling, may I drink a tiny drop of beer?

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('okay') used directly in spoken exchanges.

examples.text: А я пойду принесу выпить, окей?
examples.trans: I will go grab us something to drink, okay?

examples.text: Я уже всё решил. Одну треть на кладбище, две трети над океаном.
examples.trans: I've already sorted it all out. One third goes to the cemetery, two thirds over the ocean.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Макс Лавров? Привет, давай скорее обнимемся!
examples.trans: Max Lavrov? Hi, let's hug right away!

examples.text: Ладно, иди готовь скорее своего дорогого короля!
examples.trans: Fine, go prepare your expensive king right away!

examples.text: Гуля, подойди скорее сюда, у меня важное поручение.
examples.trans: Gulya, come over here quickly, I have an important errand.
